column3: Close to the Hebrew; הוֹד (“splendor”) is rendered “honor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “who lays the beams of his upper rooms on the waters” is rendered “He lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters.”
NKJV renders “who makes winds his messengers” as “Who makes His angels spirits,” reversing object and complement as in Hebrews 1:7.
Close to the Hebrew; the third person “he established” is rendered as address, “You who laid.”
Close to the Hebrew; בַּנְּחָלִים (“in the wadis”) is rendered “into the valleys,” and “mountains” “the hills.”
Close to the Hebrew; יִשְׁבְּרוּ (“break”) is rendered “quench.”
Close to the Hebrew; “mountains” is rendered “the hills.”
Close to the Hebrew; לַעֲבֹדַת (“for the labor”) is rendered “for the service of.”
Close to the Hebrew; יִשְׂבְּעוּ (“are satisfied”) is rendered “are full of sap.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the high mountains” is rendered “The high hills,” and “mountain goats” “the wild goats.”
Close to the Hebrew; לְמוֹעֲדִים (“for appointed times”) is rendered “for seasons.”
Close to the Hebrew; קִנְיָנֶךָ (“your creatures”) is rendered “Your possessions.”
Close to the Hebrew; רֶמֶשׂ (“creeping things”) is rendered “teeming things.”
